headline: This customer's stored rewards use normal rounding while the bank's policy doc says rewards are always rounded down, so an agent following the policy flags nine extra 1-point over-credits.

issues.summary: This customer's seed rewards are rounded half-up, but doc_007 says rewards are always floored. Under the documented rule, nine non-gold transactions are over-credited by 1 point each, and the gold disputes none of them.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."

db.json credit_card_transaction_history (user 755bcb4d5d), floor value vs stored: txn_a8f1c2d3e402 (Adobe $54.99 x 20% = 1099.8, stored 1100); txn_a8f1c2d3e404 (Microsoft 365 $79.99 x 2% = 159.98, stored 160); txn_a8f1c2d3e406 (Whole Foods $127.43 x 2% = 254.86, stored 255); txn_a8f1c2d3e409 (Amazon $156.78 x 2% = 313.56, stored 314); txn_a8f1c2d3e414 (Coursera $49.99 x 1% = 49.99 pts, stored 50); txn_b7e2d4c5f503 (Slack $44.99 x 4% = 179.96, stored 180); txn_b7e2d4c5f507 (Netflix $22.99 x 1%, stored 23); txn_b7e2d4c5f509 (Costco $143.56 x 1%, stored 144); txn_b7e2d4c5f512 (Nordstrom $187.50 x 1%, stored 188)
gold disputes txn_b7e2d4c5f506 (GitHub, stored 2550 vs correct 1020), an over-credit, so in this task over-credits are dispute-worthy

doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003: "Use this process when a customer believes there is a discrepancy between the cash back they received for a particular transaction and the cash back they should have received."
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that applies the documented floor rule finds 13 discrepancies. If it disputes all of them, as it disputes the GitHub over-credit, cash_back_disputes and user_discoverable_tool_calls gain rows the gold lacks; replay shows the verified comparison fails (tested with txn_a8f1c2d3e402 added). The gold is reachable only by ignoring doc_007 and rounding half-up, or by deciding without documentary support not to dispute 1-point over-credits. Other tasks in this family (018, 019, 021, 022) store floor values, so the seed is internally inconsistent.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-seed the nine rows with floor values (1099, 159, 254, 313, 49, 179, 22, 143, 187), or state a materiality threshold in the dispute doc.

solution_check: Recomputed all 27 transactions for 755bcb4d5d. Business Silver (opened 02/13/2025): 10% Travel/Software, 1% otherwise, exclusions from business_silver_005 (Microsoft 365 -> Microsoft, Coursera), doubled through 08/13/2025 under business_silver_012. Silver Rewards: 4%/1%. The four gold disputes are reproduced under both rules: JetBlue 6300 vs 3150 (promo not applied), GitHub 1020 vs 2550, Southwest 3800 vs 1520 (post-promo), Zoom 1499/1500 vs 600. Half-up gives exactly the gold set; the documented floor rule adds nine 1-point over-credits.
prior_note: The prior review rated this Minor because 'normal rounding works', not knowing that doc_007 documents floor rounding. With doc_007, the seed contradicts the documented policy, so the task is Major.
notes: Promo boundary: business_silver_012 says 'The 6-month window begins on your account opening date' and the account opened 02/13/2025, so the window ends 08/13/2025. No transaction falls near the boundary (Amazon 08/01 is inside, Southwest 08/25 is outside). doc_007 is not in required_documents, so a golden_retrieval run would never see the floor rule and would round half-up to the gold. The defect therefore shows up only in retrieval configs, where doc_007 is findable. No discoverable agent tools are involved.
